# Agent-Ready Web Profile (ARWP)

> ARWP is an evidence-backed interoperability resolver for discovering how a public website can actually be used by software and AI agents across ordinary web discovery, llms.txt, structured data, APIs, Agent Skills, MCP, A2A and related surfaces.

This is the canonical English agent-routing surface for the ARWP project.
Canonical technical language: English (`en`).
Localized routing surfaces are available in German (`de`) and Russian (`ru`). They translate discovery context and search vocabulary, not protocol identifiers or normative technical contracts.

## Start here

- [ARWP Resolver](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/): Public project page and resolver workflow.
- [ARWP Trust Center](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/trust/): Maintainer identity, evidence policy, security, corrections, software provenance, persistent-identifier state, external trust signals and explicit limitations.
- [Agentic Web Protocol Observatory](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/observatory/): Dated primary-source-reviewed map of MCP, A2A, WebMCP, llms.txt, Agent Skills, RFC discovery and emerging commerce mechanisms.
- [AI Crawler & Access Matrix](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/crawler-matrix/): Current official-source matrix separating AI search indexing, user-triggered retrieval and model-training controls.
- [ARWP Claims Registry](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/evidence/claims/): Stable scoped technical claims with IDs, review state, evidence and explicit limitations.
- [Resolver model](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/RESOLVER.md): How heterogeneous discovery evidence is normalized, compared and routed.
- [Profile specification](https://github.com/dkharlanau/agent-ready-web-profile/blob/main/SPEC.md): Experimental ARWP profile contract. Treat this English document as normative for project-defined semantics.
- [Conformance](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/CONFORMANCE.md): What ARWP conformance does and does not assert.
- [AI Search & Citation Profile](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/AI-SEARCH-PROFILE.md): Reusable implementation profile for original research, answer pages, evidence, trust, observability, open reuse and citation-oriented discovery surfaces.
- [Open Media & AI Reuse Pack](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/media/): Permission-free reuse guidance for designated ARWP-authored media/research assets under CC BY 4.0.

## Trust, corrections and provenance

ARWP treats trust as a set of inspectable signals rather than a score.

Current project trust surfaces establish:

- the named maintainer and canonical repository/site/citation metadata;
- an evidence model that prefers primary sources, separates owner-controlled examples from independent evidence, preserves negative results and keeps planned work distinct from active capabilities;
- a public security-reporting policy for the resolver/gateway attack surface;
- a corrections ledger where material published factual errors are recorded rather than silently rewritten;
- a publish workflow configured to create GitHub Artifact Attestation provenance for the exact npm tarball on the next npm publish;
- an OpenSSF Scorecard workflow as an external repository-practice signal;
- `CITATION.cff` prepared for durable software citation and future Zenodo archiving.

Persistent-identifier status is intentionally conservative: **no DOI is currently claimed**. The DOI module remains `planned` until Zenodo or another external provider actually issues an identifier. Do not infer a DOI from repository metadata.

Artifact provenance is not a security certificate. It can establish where/how a particular artifact was built; it does not prove that the artifact is vulnerability-free or correct. OpenSSF results likewise remain bounded external signals rather than product-quality guarantees.

## AI crawler and access policy

Do not interpret “AI access” as one boolean. ARWP separates at least three publisher decisions:

1. **Search/indexing** — may the provider crawl/index the site for AI/search result discovery?
2. **User-triggered retrieval** — may an assistant fetch the page because a user explicitly requested information from it?
3. **Training/model use** — may documented crawler/product controls permit the content to be collected/used for model-training or related non-Search uses?

The 2026-09-05 matrix covers OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity and Microsoft/Bing. Important reviewed distinctions:

- OpenAI documents `OAI-SearchBot` separately from `GPTBot`, so ChatGPT search visibility and potential model-training crawl access can be configured independently.
- Anthropic documents `Claude-SearchBot`, `Claude-User` and `ClaudeBot` as separate search, user-triggered and training roles.
- Google Search AI features use ordinary Googlebot/Search controls. `Google-Extended` is a robots product token, not a distinct request User-Agent; it does not control Google Search inclusion but does control specified Gemini training/grounding uses.
- Perplexity's current official sources are not fully consistent about `Perplexity-User` robots behavior. ARWP preserves this as `official-source-conflict` and intentionally emits no confident robots rule for it.
- Bingbot is a search/index crawler upstream of Bing/Microsoft AI experiences. Microsoft documents additional page-level robots meta / X-Robots-Tag controls for Chat/Copilot display and generative-AI training; ARWP does not invent a separate Bing training crawler.

Crawler access is separate from copyright/reuse permission. ARWP's `media/rights.json` explicitly licenses covered material for AI/ML reuse under CC BY 4.0, while crawler access is still independently controlled by robots/WAF/product rules.

Allowing a crawler does not guarantee inclusion, citation or ranking in any AI/search system.

## Protocol observatory

The observatory is a dated research surface, not a protocol popularity or readiness score. It keeps three things separate:

1. what the upstream protocol/specification currently says;
2. how the mechanism is discovered or invoked;
3. what ARWP currently supports, verifies, merely watches, or explicitly does not assess.

The 2026-09-05 snapshot covers HTTP Web Linking, llms.txt, RFC 9727 API Catalog, RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata, MCP, A2A, Agent Skills, WebMCP, Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) and Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP). The initial snapshot is frozen at `/observatory/history/2026-09-05.json`.

Important boundaries:

- a listed upstream mechanism is not automatically supported by ARWP;
- static discovery is not runtime conformance;
- authorization metadata does not grant access;
- browser-runtime WebMCP is `not-assessed` by the static resolver rather than treated as absent;
- ACP and UCP are currently watchlist items for future transaction-intent work, not implemented ARWP adapters;
- the Agent Skills core specification defines `SKILL.md`; ARWP's web-oriented discovery adapter is kept distinct from the core upstream specification.

## Verified claims

Use claim IDs when a precise reviewed statement is more useful than general project prose. Published claims are retained historically; if evidence or scope changes, a claim is superseded or withdrawn rather than silently rewritten.

- [ARWP-CLAIM-0001](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/evidence/claims/ARWP-CLAIM-0001.html): For A2A 1.0, an Agent Card is discovery metadata. A client selects a compatible entry from `supportedInterfaces[]` and uses that entry's URL; the Agent Card retrieval URL is not automatically the callable endpoint. Scope: A2A 1.0 discovery/callable-interface semantics, not reachability, authorization or provider trust.
- [ARWP-CLAIM-0002](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/evidence/claims/ARWP-CLAIM-0002.html): On the unchanged reviewed 20-site corpus measured 2026-08-28 after the general OpenAPI search-eligibility correction, `llms-aware` scored 89/100, `resolver-union` 86/100, resolver regret was 6 and uniquely-correct union cases were 0. Scope: this frozen engineering benchmark only; it is not a web-wide adoption, ranking, answer-quality, latency or token-cost claim.

Machine-readable claim objects contain structured facts, evidence links, `doesNotProve` boundaries, review dates and project-version context. The Claims Registry is active. Replayable Evidence Receipts remain a separate planned module; a reviewed claim is not itself a complete replay bundle or trust certificate.

## Canonical answers, concepts and comparisons

Use these stable pages when a direct citable answer is more useful than broad project documentation:

- [What is an agentic web resolver?](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/answers/what-is-agentic-web-resolver.html): Direct answer, scope, evidence and implementation boundaries.
- [MCP vs A2A vs WebMCP vs llms.txt](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/answers/mcp-vs-a2a-vs-webmcp-vs-llms-txt.html): Current role map for four frequently conflated layers.
- [Agentic web resolver — definition](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/concepts/agentic-web-resolver.html): Canonical ARWP project definition.
- [Resolver regret — definition](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/concepts/resolver-regret.html): Decision-quality metric used by ARWP benchmarks.
- [Discovery conflict — definition](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/concepts/discovery-conflict.html): Canonical definition for contradictory discovery evidence.
- [Static metadata vs runtime evidence](https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/compare/static-metadata-vs-runtime-evidence.html): What publisher declarations can prove versus what live protocol/browser observation can prove.

These pages are reviewed, date-stamped and explicitly mark ARWP-created vocabulary as project-defined rather than industry-standard terminology. Covered explanatory text is reusable under CC BY 4.0 with attribution.

## Reusable AI search / citation program

ARWP carries a non-normative profile that can be applied to other sites. It tracks implementation status rather than producing a readiness score.

The profile covers:

- direct answer pages for recurring questions;
- original research and negative results;
- a dated protocol observatory;
- protocol comparison pages;
- canonical concept definitions;
- stable claim identifiers and evidence receipts;
- an AI/search crawler matrix;
- a canonical trust center and corrections ledger;
- software provenance and externally issued persistent identifiers;
- independent/external trust signals with explicit limitations;
- reproducible experiments about which surfaces agents actually fetch;
- a machine-readable knowledge graph;
- reusable citation visuals;
- an open press/media reuse pack with machine-readable rights;
- external distribution with one canonical source;
- AI/search citation and referral measurement;
- localization and product history.

`planned` means intended work and must not be interpreted as a deployed capability. `active` means the surface is currently published or operated. A workflow configured for the next release is not evidence that historical artifacts already carry that provenance.

## Open media & AI reuse

Designated ARWP-authored press facts, research visuals and media assets can be reused without requesting separate permission when they are covered by the media rights manifest.

Current policy for covered material:

- license: CC BY 4.0;
- press/news/editorial/commercial reuse: permitted;
- adaptation/translation: permitted;
- AI search indexing: permitted;
- AI/ML training and dataset inclusion: permitted;
- embeddings and retrieval-augmented generation: permitted;
- summarization: permitted;
- attribution: required for public reuse; preserve the canonical source URL in dataset/model cards, provenance metadata, citations, output attribution or another reasonable attribution surface when the workflow provides one.

Preferred credit:

`Source: Agent-Ready Web Profile (ARWP) — https://dkharlanau.github.io/agent-ready-web-profile/`

Software remains Apache-2.0. Third-party logos, trademarks, screenshots, quotations and other third-party material are not included unless separately marked.

## Boundaries

ARWP is not an SEO ranking mechanism, permission layer, replacement for MCP/A2A/OAuth/OpenAPI, proof that an undeclared runtime capability exists, security certificate, or external endorsement. The AI Search & Citation Profile is likewise not a guarantee of inclusion, citation or ranking in any search/AI product. Machine-readable reuse permission applies only to material explicitly covered by the rights manifest and does not override third-party rights. Prefer observed and protocol-native evidence, publish original useful material, preserve source authority and negative results, keep planned surfaces distinct from active ones, and do not claim DOI/attestation/adoption before the relevant external evidence exists. When a localized routing surface and the canonical English technical documentation differ, use the canonical English technical documentation for project-defined semantics.
